title: WorkspaceOnboardingForm
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of MonarchTextField, MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput, MonarchRadioCardGroup and MonarchButton, with rememberSaveable state for values and validation
summary: A recipe, not a component: the form that creates a workspace, with a name, a unique username checked for availability, and a workspace type, with inline validation and a pending submit.
whenToUse: In the first-run flow of a product that needs a workspace or organization before anything else.
whenNotToUse: Not for editing an existing workspace's settings (use a settings screen with sections) and not for signing up a person (that is the account flow).
api: MonarchTextField(value = name, onValueChange = …, label = "Workspace name", errorText = nameError)
MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput(value = username, label = "Workspace username", onValueChange = …, validate = …, prefix = "@", onStatusChange = …)
MonarchRadioCardGroup(options = …, selected = type, onSelect = …, label = "Type", columns = 2)
MonarchButton(text = "Continue", onClick = …, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary, loading = creating)

options.name: name
options.description: The workspace name. The example requires 4 to 25 characters; the rule is the app's.

options.name: username
options.description: The unique handle, checked by MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput. The example allows 5 to 30 letters and digits.

options.name: type
options.description: The chosen workspace type; the example offers Creator and Business.

options.name: submitted
options.description: Set by Continue, so empty fields show their errors only after a submit.

options.name: creating
options.description: Passed to the Continue button's loading while the product creates the workspace.

states.name: invalid name
states.description: MonarchTextField shows the error once the person has typed or submitted: at least 4 and at most 25 characters.

states.name: username checking, available, taken or failed
states.description: MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput checks the local rules and the product's lookup after typing pauses and reports its status; Continue waits for Valid.

states.name: type missing
states.description: After a submit without a type, an error line in the danger strong color appears under the cards.

states.name: creating
states.description: The Continue button shows its progress indicator and reads "Loading" while the product creates the workspace.

appearance: Each part keeps its own Monarch look: the text field's input border, the username field's status colors, the radio cards' selected border and mark, the primary button. Errors use the danger strong role. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships WorkspaceOnboardingForm as one pattern with onSubmit, checkUsername, rules and messages props. On Android it is a recipe, as on iOS: the fields, rules and submit logic stay in the app's composable, so the rules (4 to 25 characters for the name, 5 to 30 letters and digits for the username) and the types (Creator and Business) are shown in the example and are not a Monarch API. The web's form error alert after a failed submit is left to the app, for example a MonarchInlineNotice above the button. The type error has no icon because Monarch bundles none; it is text.
accessibility: Each field keeps its own label, helper and error text, read by TalkBack with the field.
The username status is announced by MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput through a polite live region.
The type cards are radio buttons in a selectable group with the label.
Errors are text, not color alone.
The Continue button reads "Loading" while creating.
edgeCases: Submitting while the username is still being checked does nothing; tell the person to wait, as the catalogue page does.
At font scales of 1.5 and above, and on windows under 640dp, the two type cards stack in one column.
The values survive rotation through rememberSaveable; the username status is checked again.
